node.statement: Let Q=T_{breve-e}breve-calU with its quotient norm and A=D-breve-sigma_{breve-e}. Node 1.3.2 gives ||A+I_Q||<1. Hence T_0:=I_Q-A=2I_Q-(A+I_Q)=2(I_Q-(A+I_Q)/2) is a Banach-space isomorphism by the Neumann series, since ||(A+I_Q)/2||<1/2. Now choose any smooth chart theta at breve-e, after shrinking its domain so that breve-sigma maps it into the chart, with theta(breve-e)=0. Put E for its finite-dimensional coordinate space, S=Dtheta_{breve-e}:Q->E, b=theta o breve-sigma o theta^{-1}, and L=Db(0)=S A S^{-1}. Then T:=I_E-L=S T_0 S^{-1} is an isomorphism; no bound on ||L+I_E|| in the coordinate norm is asserted or needed. For q(x)=x-b(x), one has Dq(0)=T. Choose a norm on E (any norm makes finite-dimensional E Banach) and rho>0 with B_rho(0) in the domain of q. Because x |-> T^{-1}Dq(x) is continuous and equals I_E at 0, after decreasing rho there is c<1 such that ||T^{-1}Dq(x)-I_E||<=c throughout B_rho(0). Lem-stage1-quantitative-inverse-function applied with V=T, x_0=0, and f=q makes q injective on B_rho(0). Since breve-sigma(breve-e)=breve-e, b(0)=0 and q(0)=0, so q has no other zero there. Thus breve-e is an isolated fixed point of breve-sigma.
